around.headline: Wife, mother and lover held for murdering bedridden Bengaluru man, staged as heart attack
around.summary: Police arrested a Bengaluru woman, her mother and her lover for allegedly murdering her bedridden husband in Avalahalli and staging it as a heart attack, per Deccan Herald and The Indian Express. If a family death is sudden or unexplained, insisting on a proper medical examination rather than accepting an informal explanation is what surfaced this case.

around.summary: With Special Intensive Revision (SIR) notices still not reaching many Bengaluru households, TOI has an explainer on checking and correcting your entry directly rather than waiting for paper delivery. around.headline: Highway safety: 2 killed, 12 injured in Pune-Bengaluru crash; Salem-Bengaluru highway also snarled
around.summary: A multi-vehicle pile-up on the Pune-Bengaluru highway killed two people and injured twelve, while a separate container-lorry collision halted traffic on the Salem-Bengaluru highway, per Hindustan Times, TOI and The News Mill. If you're driving in or out of the city this weekend, build in extra buffer time and avoid overtaking on these stretches.

around.summary: Heavy processions and immersion traffic are backing up flyovers within the city and toll plazas on the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway as the festival rush continues, per Udayavani and Deccan Herald. Plan an alternate route or extra travel time if you're heading out of town this weekend.

around.summary: Private bus operators are charging as much as ₹7,999 for one-way festival-season tickets out of Bengaluru, even as the state separately weighs a broader bus fare revision, per Inshorts and TOI. Compare state-run KSRTC fares or book early before paying a surge price.

street_smart.title: You're on a weekend trek through Turahalli forest, a popular nature spot on Bengaluru's outskirts, when you come across a dumping ground of used syringes, IV bags and blood-stained gauze mixed in with dead animal carcasses — exactly what a nature content creator filmed at the same spot today. Your dog, off the leash, runs ahead and starts sniffing through the pile. What's the smartest thing to do?
street_smart.based_on: TOI Bengaluru, Sept 13 — nature content creator 'Bittu Tabahi' found dog carcasses and medical waste dumped along the Turahalli forest trail. This illegal-biomedical-waste-dumping bystander-response mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: There's no phone signal deep in the tree cover, and the nearest trailhead exit is a 15-minute walk back the way you came.

choices.text: Call your dog back and keep everyone away from the pile, photograph it from a distance without touching anything, then once you're back in signal range report the exact location to the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board's helpline and the forest department so certified biomedical-waste handlers can clear it.
choices.feedback: Correct. Biomedical waste needs certified handling under India's Biomedical Waste Management Rules — your job is to document the location and hazard, not touch it, and a report to KSPCB or the forest department is what actually triggers a proper cleanup crew.

choices.text: Pick up the worst of the syringes and soiled material yourself with your bare hands or a stick, and bag it up so no other hiker or animal steps on it before you leave.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Handling used syringes and blood-soiled waste without protective gear risks a needle-stick injury and exposure to bloodborne infections like Hepatitis or HIV — and moving it yourself doesn't stop whoever is dumping there from doing it again.

choices.text: Post photos and videos on social media tagging local authorities, and hope enough attention forces a cleanup.
choices.feedback: Risky. Public attention can help, but without a formal complaint and location report, there's no ticket number or agency actually accountable to act, and the hazard can sit there for days while it goes viral.

choices.text: Just leash your dog, move on, and avoid this stretch of the trail on future visits.
choices.feedback: Risky. That protects only you — the next hiker, child, or stray animal to pass through still faces the same needle-stick and infection risk, when a single call after your trek could get it addressed.

takeaways: Never touch used syringes, IV bags, or blood-soiled material barehanded — even a scratch carries a real risk of bloodborne infection; document and report instead.

Report illegal biomedical or industrial dumping to the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board's helpline or your local BBMP/forest office with photos and the exact location — that's what triggers a certified hazardous-waste cleanup, not a regular garbage truck.
Keep dogs leashed on unfamiliar forest trails — carcasses and biomedical waste can pass on infections through sniffing or licking.

quiz.question: How many people were killed in today's multi-vehicle crash on the Pune-Bengaluru highway?
quiz.why: Twelve others were injured in the same crash — highway pile-ups like this are a reminder to keep extra following distance in festival-week traffic.

quiz.question: Roughly how much are private operators charging for a one-way inter-city bus ticket out of Bengaluru this festival season?
quiz.why: Surge pricing on private buses is common around major festivals — comparing state-run KSRTC fares before booking can save a substantial amount.

quiz.question: By which year did Union Home Minister Amit Shah say the Uniform Civil Code would be implemented across all BJP- and NDA-ruled states?
quiz.why: Shah's remark referred to 21 states currently under BJP or NDA-partner rule; Karnataka's state government is not among them.

quiz.question: Which strait, separating Iran from the Arabian Peninsula, carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil trade?
quiz.why: Because so much oil passes through this one narrow chokepoint, any disruption there tends to move global crude prices within days.

quiz.question: Under India's Biomedical Waste Management Rules, which colour-coded bin is used for human anatomical waste and soiled items?
quiz.why: Red bins are for recyclable items like tubing, and white/translucent bins are reserved specifically for sharps like needles.
